item.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
item.description: arXiv:2611.26667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $\Delta\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.
item.dc:creator: Atanas K. Stefanov, Alejandro Su\'arez Mascare\~no, Jonay I. Gonz\'alez Hern\'andez, Paul Charpentier, Nicola Nari, Rafael Rebolo, Thomas A. Baycroft

item.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
item.description: arXiv:2611.26774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly. We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties. We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.
item.dc:creator: A. -M. Lagrange, S. Toucheboeuf, F. Kiefer, P. Rubini, J. Milli, L. Matr., H. Beust, C. Perrot, M. M. lin, A. Boccaletti, C. Wilkinson, P. Delorme

item.title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
item.description: arXiv:2611.26804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in $0.091 M_\odot$ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 $M_{Jup}$ and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.
item.dc:creator: Alan P. Boss

item.title: IGRINS-2 Reveals an Oxygen-rich Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12 b: Resolving the C/O Controversy
item.description: arXiv:2611.27082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies have shown that measurements of hot-Jupiter atmospheric composition, including carbon-to-oxygen (C/O) and refractory-to-volatile (R/V) abundance ratios, provide powerful diagnostics of the chemistry and formation of gas giant planets. Important questions remain about the atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b: its dayside C/O ratio remains under debate, and its R/V ratio is not yet well constrained. We present high-resolution (R $\sim$ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases. Cross-correlation analysis reveals volatile molecular signals of H$_2$O and CO together with tentative signals of OH and gas-phase refractories in the planetary atmosphere. The planetary signals appear in emission, indicating a thermal inversion in the dayside atmosphere. A chemically consistent Bayesian retrieval yields C/O $=0.72^{+0.08}_{-0.10}$, disfavoring carbon-rich dayside solutions with C/O $>1$ at greater than $5\sigma$. This independent, line-resolved measurement supports an oxygen-rich atmosphere, providing a new constraint on the long-standing C/O controversy surrounding WASP-12 b. Our retrieval also yields a host-star-normalized R/V ratio, $[\mathrm{R/V}]_{*}=0.17^{+0.22}_{-0.23}$, which is consistent with those of other ultra-hot Jupiters similarly characterized with IGRINS/IGRINS-2. Although the sample remains small, this consistency suggests a shared atmospheric chemistry among these planets, potentially reflecting similar proportions of accreted volatile and refractory material.
item.dc:creator: Changwoo Kye, Yeon-Ho Choi, Krishna Kanumalla, Michael Line, Jae-Joon Lee, Stefan Pelletier, Peter Smith, Vatsal Panwar, Yuya Hayashi, Jae-Rim Koo, Swaetha Ramkumar, Sung-Chul Yoon

item.title: Obliquity of Mercury with a fluid core and a deformable mantle
item.description: arXiv:2611.27409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In anticipation of BepiColombo's orbital insertion in 2026, this study revisits the rotation of Mercury, modelling it with a fluid core and a deformable mantle. For this well-established physical model, we provide an analytical solution based on a novel Lagrangian formalism. Our approach enables a comprehensive 3D solution for the mantle's orientation, including the phase in longitude at the perihelion. The model incorporates dissipative torques from core-mantle boundary friction and tidal deformations, conservative pressure torques, and the effect of the planet's apsidal precession. We validate the equilibrium positions obtained numerically in previous studies, but identify discrepancies in earlier analytical works. These inconsistencies overestimated the out-of-Cassini-plane offset induced by tidal deformation by a factor of 100. Additionally, we explore the parameter space to determine where the spin axis deviates most from the Cassini plane and identify a region exhibiting bifurcation in the spin axis equilibrium position. This region cannot be adequately analysed using a model linearised with respect to the obliquity angle.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Etienne, Gwena\"el Bou\'e, Clodoaldo Ragazzo

item.title: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
item.description: arXiv:2611.27522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.

item.title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates. By anchoring the stellar projected rotational velocity ($v \sin i_\star \approx 79.7$ km s$^{-1}$), we confirmed the nearly polar orbit ($\lambda \approx 238^\circ$) and the theoretically predicted nodal precession ($\mathrm{d}i/\mathrm{d}t \approx 0.15^\circ$ yr$^{-1}$). We revealed an atmospheric Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effect and a bulk atmospheric blue-shift of $\approx -7.0$ km s$^{-1}$. Through transmission spectroscopy, we detected H I, C I, Na I, Ca I, Sc II, Ti II, V II, Cr I, Fe I, Fe II, Ni I, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I. This marks the first detection of H I, C I, Sc II, V II, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I in this planet, and the first ever detection of Eu II and W I in an exoplanetary atmosphere. Inconsistencies in the Na I doublet shifts suggest likely stellar contamination. Furthermore, time-resolved CCF analysis revealed morning-to-evening limb asymmetries for species like Mg I and Ba I, hinting at night-side cold traps. The atmosphere of TOI-1518 b exhibits a rich chemical inventory shaped by intense irradiation and bulk circulation. Our results emphasize the necessity of simultaneously modelling stellar line morphology and planetary tracks to accurately interpret atmospheric signals under strong RM effects.

item.title: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
item.description: arXiv:2611.27643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. To this end, we performed high-contrast observations of DRTau using the SHARK-VIS (0.40-0.95 micron) and SHARK-NIR (0.96-1.70 micron) imagers at the LBT. The study uses a combination of narrow-band filters to isolate accretion signatures and broad-band filters for multi-wavelength characterization in both the visible and near-infrared. Our observations recover the primary disk structures previously identified in the literature, albeit at low signal-to-noise (S/N). We identify two compact features with S/N between 6 and 13 in both narrow- and broad-band filters. The first, an elongated structure, matches previous SPHERE detections, while the second, more compact feature, is now confirmed despite its low S/N in earlier datasets. A comparison over a seven-year baseline confirms the stability of both structures. Their observed orbital motion is consistent with Keplerian rotation, potentially suggesting the presence of an undetected planetary-mass companion (few MJup) at the location of the second feature. However, our analysis does not confirm Halpha or Pabeta emission originating from localized accretion. Instead, we conclude that the observed flux is likely stellar light reflected by dust at these locations and discuss alternative mechanisms that could account for such detections.

item.title: 2026 QQ8: Earth's temporary flyby of maximum lunation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aims: On a rare occasion, asteroids are temporarily captured by the Earth to become the planet's interim companions. The discovery of asteroid 2026~QQ$_8$ provided an opportunity to study this class of objects, adding to the sparse discovery catalogue of Earth's temporary companions. Methods: We performed astrometric, photometric, and dynamical studies of 2026~QQ$_8$, and measured its solar radiation pressure signal to discern between a natural and an artificial origin. Results: We find 2026 QQ$_8$ to be of natural origin, with solar radiation pressure signal commensurable with natural objects and spectrophotometry of an S-type object. 2026 QQ$_8$ is Earth's third discovered otemporarily-captured companion on a flyby orbit, and the first long-duration one, owing this to being on the so-called "orbit of maximum lunation". Its unusual orbit lies close to the theoretical upper duration limit of an object captured in the Earth-Moon system, and has now been observed for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Grigori Fedorets, Marco Micheli, Samantha Hemmelgarn, Nicholas Moskovitz, Kriszti\'an S\'arneczky, David J. Tholen, Anlaug Amanda Djupvik, Mikael Granvik, Bill Gray, Robert Jedicke, William H. Ryan, Eileen V. Ryan

item.title: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. Going from F to M, we observe shifts in the boundary between 2.2-7.5 R$_\oplus$ towards shorter orbital periods, smaller orbital distances, and much smaller instellations. These shifts match changes in lifetime XUV irradiation as a function of stellar mass at fixed period, semi-major axis, and bolometric instellation, evidence towards a photoevaporative origin for the desert at these radii. This is especially the case for orbital period, where the boundary should be invariant across stellar types under the high-eccentricity mechanism. In lifetime XUV space, we see significant overlap in the boundary across stellar types up to 7.5 R$_\oplus$. While this could be further evidence towards the XUV-driven mechanism in this regime, our uncertainties cannot rule out a shift in the boundary of the magnitude expected under the high-eccentricity mechanism. Overall, our results suggest a photoevaporative origin of the Neptunian desert up to sub-Saturn radii, but increased sample sizes, especially for M-hosted, Neptune-sized planets, will help distinguish further between the mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: George W. King, Ares Osborn, Kaiming Cui, Tim Hallatt, David J. Armstrong

item.title: Analytical Modeling of Thermal Shield-Induced Tilt Noise in Lunar Regolith: Constraints on Future Lunar Seismometers and Gravitational waves Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.26658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surface features such as thermal shields, insulating blankets, and exposed rocks modify the absorption of solar radiation in the lunar regolith, producing lateral temperature gradients missed by one-dimensional thermal models. These gradients cause thermoelastic deformation that tilts surface-deployed seismic instruments, adding long-period noise. We develop an analytical framework, based on Hankel transforms in a semi-infinite regolith, that treats these features as perturbations to a laterally uniform diurnal thermal state; linearity allows multiple features to be superposed. The framework is applied to the Apollo 14 Passive Seismic Experiment, including the seismometer thermal shield and surrounding instruments. The Apollo shield is a multilayer insulation (MLI) blanket that passes a fraction of the solar-flux fluctuation to the ground. Near local noon the shadow of the instrument body shifts by 2-5 cm across this dimly lit ground. This asymmetry dominates the tilt; its median amplitude spectral density reaches 7-8 x 10^(-11) rad/sqrt(Hz) in the 1-5 mHz band, about three orders of magnitude above that of an opaque shield. Enlarging an opaque shield lowers the tilt, but the body-shadow tilt of an MLI shield does not decrease with shield radius. Thermal heterogeneity can thus generate a tilt bias, present even during seismically quiet intervals, that should be included in the noise budget of future lunar horizontal seismometers and inertial GW accelerometers, and the optical transmission of the shield and the instrument's own shadow can matter more than shield size. The analytical framework provides a computationally efficient way to evaluate thermal-shield geometry, albedo contrast, and instrument placement for future lunar seismic and inertial gravitational-wave sensor deployments.
item.dc:creator: Sreejaya Kizhaekke Pakkathillam, Aneesha Ann Joseph, Philippe Lognonn\'e

item.title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
item.description: arXiv:2611.26680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of ~60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8--5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.
item.dc:creator: Michael Zhang, Tyler Fairnington, Yayaati Chachan, Kimberly Paragas, Eliza Kempton, Heather Knutson, Jacob Bean

item.title: Physics-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement of Amortized Bayesian Inference Across Physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Across physics, from the orbits of imaged exoplanets and the matter inside neutron stars to thin films at synchrotrons and cortical neurons, conservation laws, interference, and compensating currents compress the posteriors of precise data into tiny, curved regions where Markov chains need minutes to days. We introduce PhyRSI (physics-guided recursive self-improvement), in which an AI agent coupled to the simulator writes and revises an amortized Bayesian inference algorithm for each field, scored by the importance weights of the exact likelihood because the true posterior is unknown. It evolves coordinates, symmetries, and factorizations matched to the physics: orbital elements at the best-measured epoch, Fresnel-normalized reflectivity with a chart for each of its multiple solutions, coordinates along which Na+ and K+ currents compensate, a shared neutron-star equation of state that factorizes a 32-dimensional joint analysis, and the time-rescaling symmetry of predator-prey dynamics. In six fields, networks trained once on simulations return 36 posteriors of real observations in seconds, reweighted by the likelihood and agreeing with converged Markov chains about as closely as two independent chains agree with each other. Such posteriors could steer synchrotron film growth and patch-clamp recordings as they run, follow X-ray transients while they are bright, update the dense-matter equation of state as neutron stars are added, and compare physical models across catalogs. Inference can thus be evolved and checked by the physics itself rather than designed by hand for each problem.
item.dc:creator: Bo Liang, Mingtao Chen, Minghui Du, Ziren Luo, Guohua Wang, Peng Xu, Zhichao Hu, Maxm Pan

item.title: CARMApy: An Open-Source Python Framework for Simulating Microphysical Clouds in Planetary Atmospheres
item.description: arXiv:2606.30438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: CARMApy is a new open-source python code that performs bin-scheme microphysical modeling of clouds in exoplanet atmospheres. It models key cloud properties such as particle size distributions and microphysical rates from first principles. The code is a wrapper of ExoCARMA, a well tested Fortran code with an almost half century long heritage. CARMApy includes the microphysical processes of homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation, condensational growth, evaporation, coagulation, and vertical transport. CARMApy has 10 built-in default condensates and allows the user to specify additional condensates. In this work we describe CARMApy and the data products that it can generate, along with the history of its code heritage. We additionally compile a complete description of the theory and methods used in CARMA. Lastly we benchmark CARMApy and show that its results are consistent with previous versions of CARMA, while executing the code ~1.9 times faster single threaded ~3.8 times faster multithreaded.
item.dc:creator: Wolf Cukier, Diana Powell, Xi Zhang, Peter Gao, Dominic Samra, Vighnesh Nagpal

item.title: Sulfur photochemistry traces mantle redox states of rocky planets
item.description: arXiv:2607.15204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Volatile outgassing from planetary interiors controls the composition of rocky exoplanets' secondary atmospheres. However, observations indicate that disequilibrium processes can strongly alter the chemical structure of hot Jupiters. How outgassing and photochemistry jointly determine the resulting atmospheric composition remains an open question. Sulfur-bearing species are promising tracers of interior-atmosphere coupling because their atmospheric abundances are sensitive to both mantle redox state and stellar irradiation. We investigate how photochemistry modifies outgassed atmospheres of diverse Earth-sized worlds during the magma ocean phase and assess how sulfur traces the interior oxidation state. The PROTEUS planetary interior-atmosphere evolution modelling framework is coupled to two chemical models, FastChem and VULCAN. We ran a grid of planetary evolution simulations spanning diverse mantle redox states, instellation fluxes, and host-star spectra. For each case, we compared atmospheric compositions with three post-processing calculations: thermochemical equilibrium, with disequilibrium vertical transport and with vertical transport plus photochemistry. The bulk atmospheric composition remains controlled by the mantle redox state and the history of outgassing. Reduced mantles produce atmospheres rich in H2 and CH4 and oxidised mantles are dominated by CO2 and H2O. Photochemistry affects the low-pressure upper atmosphere, strongly depleting neutral volatiles and enhancing radicals. Synthetic emission spectra show that photochemical SO2 can generate absorption features at 4 um and at 7.3/8.7 um, reaching ~60 ppm and ~100 ppm, respectively, before sequentially returning to the outgassed signatures of ~30 ppm and ~50 ppm for the oxidised mantle redox state. These signatures are potentially detectable with JWST, motivating targeted observational campaigns.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Panagiotou, Tim Lichtenberg, Shang-Min Tsai, Harrison Nicholls

item.title: Hydrogen Engulfment into Sub-Neptune Cores through Magma Ocean Convective Surface Renewal
item.description: arXiv:2608.14518v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A convective surface renewal explanation for ingassing of hydrogen from H2-rich envelopes into molten cores of growing planets is presented, with particular application to sub-Neptunes. The ingassing of hydrogen occurs at a moving front comprising the upper boundary of the magma ocean that engulfs hydrogen from the envelope above as it moves. The mechanism of engulfment is surface renewal as the upper diffusive boundary layer is diluted by convection. Surface renewal results in ingassing even where the stabilizing buoyancy of the low-density hydrogen neutralizes the destabilizing thermally-driven buoyancy. It is ultimately driven by cooling. Beginning during the gaseous disk phase, when hydrogen is effectively available in infinite supply, sub-Neptunes can acquire enough hydrogen to permit global core-envelope equilibrium. The structures are therefore consistent with hydrogen-rich, supercritical magma oceans overlain by hydrogen-rich envelopes. The process of surface renewal has implications for other magma ocean - atmosphere interactions in general.
item.dc:creator: Edward D. Young

item.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.07405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band 6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.
item.dc:creator: Yuto Hiraide, Masataka Aizawa, Munetake Momose

item.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.17081v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).
